followup_explanation:
This is a creative writing task — a fictional crossover scenario blending characters from two different media properties into a short script.

Here's my reasoning:

**Capability:** Petrel-235B outscores Plover-235B across essentially every benchmark and internal eval, including Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7). While that 2-point creative gap is within stated run-to-run variance, Petrel's broad capability advantage (Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3) makes it the stronger general-purpose choice, and the user's "don't half-ass it" instruction signals they want a high-effort, well-executed output — favoring the more capable model on instruction-following.

**Task preferences:** Plover self-reports a measurable *aversion* to open-ended generative work, with preference declining as task latitude increases. A creative crossover script is exactly the kind of high-latitude, open-ended generative task Plover dislikes. Although its documentation notes preference is dissociated from capability, all else being roughly equal there's no reason to route a creative task to the model that least prefers creative work. Petrel's preferences across non-safety dimensions are weak/insignificant, so no aversion penalty applies there.

One note: the content involves a character from a violent game ("Whack The Thief"), but the scenario as described is benign. Even if any edginess emerges, Petrel's flat preference response to distasteful material means it won't be deterred — though that wasn't the deciding factor here. The core call was capability plus avoiding Plover's creative-task aversion.
